cards.explanation: The answer is False. Isaiah says the LORD's arm is "…not too short to save…" and His ear isn't too dull to hear either. So whatever has gone quiet, it isn't because He can't reach or can't listen. Hold onto that, friends. The rest of the passage depends on it.

The answer is their iniquities. Isaiah says, "…your iniquities have built barriers between you and your God…" He adds that their sins have hidden His face from them. Picture a wall the people stacked up themselves, brick by brick, with nobody else holding the trowel.

The answer is lies, friends. Isaiah says, "your lips have spoken lies, and your tongue mutters injustice." Right alongside the stained hands, the mouth is in on it too. Hands and lips both get called out.

The answer is no one, bakers. Isaiah says, "No one calls for justice; no one pleads his case honestly." That's a heavy line, and Isaiah says it plainly. Nobody gets left out, and he says it again right after, that they "…rely on empty pleas…" (Isaiah 59:4).
The answer is they die, friends. Isaiah says, "Whoever eats their eggs will die…" And if you crack one open, "…a viper is hatched." I don't know about you, but I'm checking every carton from now on.

The answer is clothing, bakers. Isaiah says, "Their cobwebs cannot be made into clothing, and they cannot cover themselves with their works." I've worn an apron through a lot of flour storms, and I promise it was never made of cobweb. Their works can't cover them either.
The answer is True, friends. Isaiah says, "Their feet run to evil; they are swift to shed innocent blood." Notice the word run. They're not wandering toward it or stumbling into it.
The answer is peace, friends. Isaiah says, "no one who treads on them will know peace." He'd already said that "The way of peace they have not known…" Crooked paths don't lead there.
The answer is justice, bakers. The voice says, "…justice is far from us, and righteousness does not reach us." It's a heavy thing to say out loud. I think that's why the switch to "us" lands so hard.

The answer is the blind, friends. The voice says, "Like the blind, we feel our way along the wall, groping like those without eyes." You know that late-night walk to the kitchen with the lights off? Hand on the wall, praying you miss the furniture. It's that, only far more serious.
The answer is False, friends. The voice says, "We stumble at midday as in the twilight…" Even in full daylight, they're tripping like it's dusk. That tells you how deep the gloom is.

The answer is False, friends. The voice says, "We hope for justice, but find none, for salvation, but it is far from us." They're hoping, and it hasn't arrived. Keep that in mind, because this isn't where it ends.
The answer is their sins, bakers. The voice says, "…our sins testify against us." Nobody else had to be called to the stand. Their own sins do the talking.
The answer is True, bakers. The voice says, "Our transgressions are indeed with us, and we know our iniquities…" They name it themselves. I think that honest moment matters.
The answer is heart, friends. The voice confesses "…conceiving and uttering lies from the heart." So the lies don't just come out of the mouth. They start deeper in.
The answer is in the public square, bakers. Isaiah says, "…truth has stumbled in the public square…" Not in private, but in a public place. That's where Isaiah puts the stumble.
The answer is False, bakers. Isaiah says truth stumbled, and "…honesty cannot enter." The door is shut on it. And a sad scene like that is exactly what sets up what the LORD does next.

The answer is that there was no justice, friends. Isaiah says, "The LORD looked and was displeased that there was no justice." He saw it, and it displeased Him. That's the reason the next verses move the way they do.

The answer is His own arm, bakers. Isaiah says, "So His own arm brought salvation…" This is the same arm Isaiah said at the start is "…not too short to save…" (Isaiah 59:1). Here it is, doing the saving.
The answer is a cloak of zeal, friends. Isaiah says He "…wrapped Himself in a cloak of zeal." Breastplate, helmet, garments, and now a cloak. That's the full outfit.
The answer is deeds, bakers. Isaiah says, "So He will repay according to their deeds…" It's about what people actually did. The word is deeds.
The answer is True, friends. Isaiah says, "So shall they fear the name of the LORD where the sun sets, and His glory where it rises." West and east, both named. His name reaches all the way around.
The answer is True, bakers. Isaiah says, "For He will come like a raging flood, driven by the breath of the LORD." The breath of the LORD is what drives it. That's a lot of force.

The answer is Redeemer, friends. The LORD declares, "The Redeemer will come to Zion…" After all that darkness in this passage, I think that's good news. Just a few verses before, the people say salvation "…is far from us," and here is a promise that Someone will come.

The answer is those who turn from transgression, bakers. The LORD says the Redeemer comes "…to those in Jacob who turn from transgression…" The door is open to those who turn. Jacob here is the people called by the name Israel (Isaiah 48:1).
The answer is His Spirit, friends. The LORD says, "My Spirit will not depart from you…" That's a promise. And it comes with His words staying in their mouths too.

The answer is False, friends. The LORD says His words will not depart from your mouth "…or from the mouths of your children and grandchildren, from now on and forevermore…" Children, then grandchildren, then onward. It's a promise with no end date.
